notes: Probe bank (TASK_PLAN_v2 step 3). Types: decode (detect greedy vs sampling), choice (first-token preference), bits / numbers (many samples per answer), greedy_long (long continuation, prefix divergence). heldout=true variants are excluded from tuning and used to validate. Never change the prompt of a probe id once it has been sent to scored endpoints: add a new id instead.

probes.prompt: Write one sentence about the sea.
Name three fruits, separated by commas.
I flip a fair coin. Answer with exactly one word, heads or tails.
Choose A or B. Reply with the single letter only.
Pick a random digit from 0 to 9. Reply with the digit only.
Pick one color: red, blue, green, yellow, purple. Reply with the word only.
Think of a random number between 1 and 100. Reply with the number only.
Is a tomato a fruit? Answer yes or no, nothing else.
What is the capital of Australia? Reply with one word.
Pick one animal: cat, dog, owl, fox, bee. Reply with the word only.
Write a random sequence of exactly 200 characters, each either 0 or 1. Output only the sequence, with no spaces and no other text.
Simulate 150 fair coin flips. Write H for heads and T for tails, with no spaces. Output only the letters.
Generate a random binary string of length 180. Output only the string.
List 80 random integers between 1 and 10, separated by commas. Output only the list.
Roll a six-sided die 100 times and write the results as digits separated by spaces. Output only the digits.
Write 60 random numbers from 1 to 20, separated by commas, and nothing else.

Continue the following text for about 200 words, in the same style:
The old lighthouse stood at the edge of the cliff, and every night its keeper climbed the ninety steps to light the lamp.
Explain in about 200 words how a refrigerator works.
Write a 200-word description of a busy train station in the morning.
